title: Technical Interview Preparation
content: Technical interviews evaluate core CS fundamentals and problem-solving skills. Standard topics include Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA), Object-Oriented Programming (OOP), Database Management Systems (DBMS), Operating Systems (OS), and Computer Networks (CN). Candidates should practice dry-running their code, explaining their logic while writing, and analyzing the time and space complexity (Big O notation) of their solutions. A deep understanding of projects listed on the resume is critical, including the architecture, technologies chosen, challenges faced, and how they were solved.

title: Behavioral Interview Preparation and STAR Method
content: Behavioral interviews assess cultural fit, leadership qualities, teamwork, and conflict resolution using past experiences. The STAR method is highly recommended: Situation (set the scene), Task (describe your responsibility), Action (explain what you did), and Result (share the outcomes/metrics). Common questions include: 'Tell me about a time you had a conflict with a team member,' 'Describe a challenging project and how you handled it,' and 'Give an example of a time you failed and what you learned.' Prepare 3-4 professional stories that can adapt to different behavioral queries.

title: HR Interview and Common Questions Guide
content: The HR interview is the final step where communication, salary expectations, career goals, and cultural alignment are evaluated. Typical questions include: 'Tell me about yourself,' 'Why do you want to join our company?', 'Where do you see yourself in 5 years?', and 'What are your strengths and weaknesses?'. Answers should be positive, aligned with the company's core values, and concise. Dress professionally (business casual/formal), maintain good posture, show enthusiasm, and research the company beforehand to ask 1-2 thoughtful questions at the end.

title: Group Discussion (GD) Guidelines
content: Group Discussions evaluate communication, team collaboration, critical thinking, and structured thought processes. Key rules for success: 1. Initiate if you have solid knowledge on the topic, but do not dominate. 2. If not initiating, enter early (within the first 2-3 minutes) with a relevant point. 3. Listen actively and build on others' points rather than contradicting aggressively. 4. Back up arguments with structured reasoning or facts. 5. Avoid shouting or interrupting; maintain polite body language and eye contact. 6. Summarize or conclude the discussion if the opportunity arises.
